name: YARD-SQL
tagline: Cologne-built SQL-92 RDBMS for UNIX and Linux from YARD Software (c. 1996-2012); discontinued.
description: YARD-SQL was a commercial relational database server from YARD Software GmbH of Cologne, Germany, one of the few full RDBMSs available for Linux in the late 1990s. It implemented the SQL-2 standard, stored procedures and triggers based on the draft SQL-3 specification, BLOB and TEXT types and physical and logical logging, and managed raw-disk database spaces in a style familiar to Informix OnLine administrators. Clients connected via ODBC, JDBC, embedded SQL for C, Perl and PHP, and a free single-user Private Edition was offered for evaluation. dbdb.io dates the product from 1996 to 2012; the vendor's site no longer carries it.
statusNote: No longer offered; dbdb.io lists 2012 as its end year and yard.de no longer hosts the product. Use PostgreSQL or another maintained RDBMS.

pricing.notes: Historic pricing; a free single-user Private Edition was limited to small databases.

strengths: Full SQL-2 RDBMS on Linux when the big vendors had none
Stored procedures and triggers ahead of the SQL:1999 standard
weaknesses: Raw-disk space management required careful sizing
useCases: History of commercial databases on early Linux
Maintaining legacy applications built on it
